nse:106830108.question: What had management said on recent calls about revenue and margins for this period, and does this result match it?
nse:106830108.answer: Management did not give specific quarterly guidance for Q2 FY27. In November 2025, management projected FY26 revenue around ₹12,500 crore with about 5% growth the coming year (FY27), average margins around 15% plus, or 12% to 15% for new projects. Q2 FY27's reported 16.5% revenue decline and 8.1% EBITDA margin fall well below these annual ranges.

evidence.quote: We anticipate that this year, we will have revenue of approximately INR 12,500 crores or so. And the coming year also, we should have may be another 5% growth over that
If it is some newer vessels, it may not necessarily be that high. But on an average, we can anticipate around 15% plus margins
But that will not be the case for the new projects coming in, where we are booking the actual value of production. And in that case, we expect that the margins will be around 12% to 15%

nse:106823051.question: What has management said about this on its recent calls?
nse:106823051.answer: Management did not discuss any distrust of intermediate CAs, root CA distrust, or key generation flaws. The closest discussion occurred in the Q4 FY26 call, where management stated that a Google policy change regarding multi-purpose and new root certificates had no impact because existing roots remained trusted while new roots were queued.

evidence.quote: Our new roots have been submitted some time back

So, nothing stops for us because our existing roots are already trusted on Google and we basically have a transition period where the existing roots will continue to work until the new roots are accepted by Google
So, there is really no impact as such

nse:106829089.question: What had management said on recent calls about revenue and margins for this period, and does this result match it?
nse:106829089.answer: Management said in May 2026 that consolidated revenue for FY26 reached 1,829 crore and EBITDA reached 255 crore, with Q4 EBITDA margins reaching 19.5%. In August 2026, management reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of 429 crore and EBITDA of 46 crore. The Q2 FY27 results of 803.1 crore revenue and 14.1% EBITDA margin show strong sequential and year-on-year growth.

evidence.quote: FY '26 was a pivotal year for Nazara. Revenue reached INR 1,829 crores and EBITDA grew 66% to INR 255 crores, our highest ever, with Q4 EBITDA margins reaching 19.5%, - almost doubling on a year-on-year basis
Consolidated revenue came in at INR 429 crores, and EBITDA was INR 46 crores

nse:106823393.question: What had management said on recent calls about revenue and margins for this period, and does this result match it?
nse:106823393.answer: Management stated in October 2026 that food delivery margins are expected to remain flattish over the next 1 or 2 years as they reinvest in growth, and consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 reached ₹24,138.0 crore with an EBITDA margin of 3.1%, matching their focus on balanced profitability.

evidence.quote: Directionally, we want to maintain margins broadly and reinvest in growth as much as it makes sense to continue to drive the growth upwards
It's hard to project or comment on margin trajectory every quarter but broadly, over the next 1 or 2 years, we expect the margins to remain flattish

nse:106810133.question: What has management said about debt, leverage and its credit profile?
nse:106810133.answer: Management stated that core infrastructure net external debt is about INR 45,000 crores ($5 billion), supported by a regulatory asset base of under $4 billion. For metals, materials, and mining, net external debt is about $2 billion against $6 billion in operating assets. Core infra leverage is guided between 3.5x and 4.5x, with the consolidated leverage ratio at 3.9x in the Q4 FY26 call (April 2026).

evidence.quote: for example, in core infra, which is platform, we have a net external debt of, say, INR45,000 crores, which is about just under $5 billion. Against that, the regulatory asset base itself is just under $4 billion. So it is heavily supported by the regulatory asset base.

the metals, materials and mining, we have a net external debt of about $2 billion, against where we call our operating assets, which are roughly around about $6 billion. So we keep a low or very conservative leverage profile on the metal, materials and mining side, given the volatilities we face in those businesses.

our core infra will track the core infra. So we guide to that in the core infra while we are growing, we will be closer to the 3.5 to 4.5 range. And obviously, we'll be lower in relation to the mining.

nse:106805308.question: What has management said on recent calls about leadership, succession or this role?
nse:106805308.answer: Management announced that the RBI approved Mr. Anup Bagchi as Managing Director & CEO of HDFC Bank for a three-year term effective October 27, 2026, replacing Mr. Sashidhar Jagdishan, as stated by the Board and in the Q2 FY27 earnings call in October 2026.

evidence.quote: I'm really grateful to the Board for the trust placed in me as MD and CEO

I'll also leave behind in the hands of an able team spread across various levels in the organization throughout the country, led by a new and an able leader, and I welcome Anup at this juncture heartily to the institution as well

nse:106819733.question: What has management said about raising money: how much, why, and what it is for?
nse:106819733.answer: Management stated in October 2026 that Persistent Systems plans to raise USD 1.25 billion through both debt and equity as part of its long-term financing strategy to replace the Euro 1.4 billion 18-month bridge loan used for the Nagarro acquisition. Of this, USD 450 million will be raised via equity, QIP, or equity-linked instruments.

evidence.quote: In terms of financing, we intend replacing the Euro 1.4 billion 18-month bridge loan with longer tenure, capital and favorable terms
As a part of this long-term financing strategy, we will be raising USD 1.25 billion in terms of both debt and equity
Out of this, USD 450 million will be raised through equity, qualified institutional placement or equity-linked instruments like FCCB or combination of similar instruments

nse:106831929.question: What had management said on recent calls about revenue and margins for this period, and does this result match it?
nse:106831929.answer: Management stated on recent calls that post-stabilization, Navi Mumbai Airport, Kutch Copper, and Ganga Expressway are expected to add well over INR 3,000 crores to EBITDA. evidence.quote: In the next fiscal year, AEL is set to unlock EBITDA from Navi Mumbai Airport, Kutch Copper and Ganga Expressway, which are expected to add over INR3,000 crores EBITDA to AEL
In the coming period, first, AEL will unlock EBITDA from Navi Mumbai, Kutch Copper and Ganga Expressway. Post stabilization, these 3 assets are expected to add well over INR3,000 crores to EBITDA
